items.definition: the time of day, usually in the morning or late afternoon, when large numbers of people are traveling to or from work, causing congestion on roads and public transport
items.example: I avoid driving during rush hour because the traffic on the motorway is absolutely terrible.

items.definition: occurring or found frequently; widespread or ordinary; not rare or unusual
items.example: It's common for people to feel nervous before an important exam.

items.definition: a reflexive pronoun used when the subject and object of a sentence refer to the same male person or animal; also used for emphasis
items.example: The manager himself admitted that the project had been poorly planned from the start.

items.definition: during the hours of darkness; in the period after sunset and before sunrise
items.example: The city looks completely different at night when all the buildings are lit up.

items.definition: the activity of looking after someone else's child or children for a period of time, usually while the parents are away
items.example: She earns extra money babysitting for families in her neighbourhood on weekends.

items.definition: a statement indicating that the speaker and others have not arrived on time; they will arrive after the expected or appointed time
items.example: We are late for the meeting because the train was delayed.

items.definition: feeling or expressing remorse or shame for having done something wrong; responsible for or deserving blame for an offence or wrongdoing
items.example: She felt guilty about not calling her grandmother for weeks, so she visited her the next day.
items.prepositionSentence: He was found guilty ___ fraud after the court case lasted three months.
items.wordFormationSentence: She looked away ___ when her mother asked if she'd eaten the cake.

items.definition: to express regret or ask forgiveness for something you have done wrong; to make an apology
items.example: He apologized for being rude to his colleague and sent her a sincere email explaining the pressure he'd been under.
items.prepositionSentence: You should apologize ___ breaking her phone; she's been very upset about it.
items.wordFormationSentence: His ___ tone suggested he genuinely regretted what he'd said.

items.definition: accountable or answerable for one's actions; having the duty to manage or organize something; trustworthy and reliable
items.example: As the project manager, she's responsible for ensuring all deadlines are met and the budget stays within limits.
items.prepositionSentence: Who is responsible ___ organizing the team-building event this year?
items.wordFormationSentence: He showed great ___ when he admitted his mistake rather than blaming others.

items.definition: a discourse marker used to introduce what the speaker believes or has interpreted based on the information they have, often with a degree of caution or humility
items.example: As I understand, the company is planning to relocate its headquarters to Manchester next year.

items.definition: a piece of equipment or a tool designed to perform a specific function or task; a machine or apparatus
items.example: Modern smartphones are incredibly powerful devices that can do almost everything a computer can do.

items.definition: individual actions or measures taken toward achieving a goal; a series of progressions; also, a structure with stairs for climbing or descending
items.example: The government has announced several steps to reduce unemployment, including retraining programmes for workers in declining industries.

items.definition: to remove footwear from one's feet; the action of unshod one's shoes
items.example: Please take off your shoes before entering the house, as it's traditional in this culture.
items.collocationSentence: ___ off your shoes and put on some comfortable slippers.

items.definition: the remaining stubs or butts of cigarettes after they have been smoked; discarded smoking remains
items.example: The street corner was littered with cigarette ends, indicating that people often waited there for the bus.
